newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico to hold first National Rice Fair in Nov.
newsitem.headline: Mexico to hold first National Rice Fair in Nov.

text.p: Mexico plans to stage its first National Rice Fair from November 16 to 24 in an attempt to strengthen ties in one of Mexico's most diverse sectors.

"Our aim is to strengthen productive relationships in the sector in the development and the promotion of rice as a basic product," said Erick Alejandro Castro Ibarra, president of the organising committee.

The Mexican Rice Council, which represents the country's 23 rice growers and the 23 major businesses that control 98 percent of all rice sales, will hold its annual congress at the Fair which will be in the town of Jojutla in the southern state of Morelos.

Growers, industrialists, businessmen, academics, traders, investigators and consumers are all expected to attend the gathering, with daily seminars, gastronomic shows and commercial and industrial expositions.

Jojutla is Mexico's most famous rice-growing town and is known as "The Land of the Rice". Local growers traditionally achieve the highest yields per hectare in the country and the rice council has certified Jojutla rice one of the highest quality rices in the country.
